public_primary_references.identity: Official QEMU repository tagv1.7.2; immutable commit/blob not established by this read-only review
observations: State line134 is uint32_t dbg_ctrl. Read lines277–278 returns it. Write lines407–409 stores val under the unlocked guard at363.
Lock/unlock use low16-bit keys0x767b/0xdf0d. The reset callback155–236 restores lockval but never assigns dbg_ctrl or clears the union.
Thus this callback preserves prior dbg_ctrl writes. Zero at construction depends on zero-initialized QOM allocation, not a demonstrated register-reset assignment.
The callbacks ignore access size. Do not infer physical partial-access behavior or silently broaden a new32-bit-only reference profile.

trm_findings.finding: The address map names F8000500 as CoreSight SoC debug control. This is a range summary, not a field-level behavioral table.
No DBG_CTRL field definition was found. This is a search result, not proof that no independent document exists.

trm_findings.location: DevC CTRL F8007000, printedpp964–967; LOCK F8007004,pp967–968
trm_findings.finding: SPNIDEN/SPIDEN/NIDEN/DBGEN/DAP_EN and sticky DBG_LOCK are in the separate device-configuration block. Their fields must not be assigned to SLCR0x500 by analogy.

The security policy can clear OCM/caches, reset PL and lock PS until power-on reset. DAP enable conflicts with a JTAG-disable eFuse can trigger this behavior. Secure-boot debug defaults and DevC lock state are separate constraints.

proposed_contract.defensible_scope: An explicitly named historical-QEMU reference register, after exact source pinning, can advance an original-ROM diagnostic. It cannot establish actual S9 silicon behavior.
proposed_contract.storage: Full32-bit raw write/readback, gated by existing SLCR lock; no guessed bit effects.
proposed_contract.reset: Preserve historical callback behavior if claiming reuse. If cold/reset-zero policy is chosen instead, record it as a separate adaptation and test it; do not label it unchanged prior behavior.
unsupported: Physical bit layout and reserved-bit masks
tests_before_execution: Cold instance plus full-word write/readback under explicit profile
Locked writes do not alter stored word; correct/incorrect unlock and relock keys
Warm reset relocks access and preserves stored word if restoring the inspected historical callback
Negative partial/unaligned accesses preserve state if the new profile declares them unsupported
Default strict model still rejects the access and no host debug service is exposed

next_action: Owner acquires the exact pre-rewrite QEMU file and allocation/reset evidence, then stages a narrow opt-in reference with its reset policy and tests. Continue original ROM diagnostic with unchanged evidence gates.
